transcript.content:
hey, i'm berry. i help people turn their dreams into pictures, but right now i'm just here to listen.

tell me about your dream, however it comes back to you.
there was this girl standing with me by the autoclave, and then she walked off to the other side of the room.

a girl by the autoclave, then she just walks away to the other side of the room.

what happened after that?
when she came back, her head was gone and it was this block of glittering ice sitting on her shoulders instead.

that's such a strange, quiet image. a block of glittering ice just sitting there where her head was.

did it feel like something was wrong, or was it just how she was now?
it didn’t feel wrong really. she just stood in front of me, quite natural, not saying anything.

not saying anything, just standing there with that ice. it's like the dream didn't make a fuss about it either.

what were you doing while she stood there?
i was just watching it. the ice started to melt a bit, little channels opening up and the sharp edges rounding away.

little channels opening up, the sharp edges softening. that sounds slow, almost hypnotic.

did any light catch the ice in a way you noticed?
i don’t remember any light on it, really. just that it kept changing, the sculpturing went on fast after the first trickle.

so it went from a slow trickle to something faster, the whole thing reshaping itself.

how did it end up, the ice block?
it ended as a horse's head. a beautifully molded one, with eyes, ears, and nostrils carved out clear.

a horse's head, beautifully molded, all the details clear. that's quite a shift from a block of ice.

how did you feel seeing that on her shoulders?
it didn’t feel frightening. the melting was more like carving than falling apart.

like the ice knew what it was becoming all along.

where were you two when this happened?
by the autoclave, in the room we’d been talking in.

so it's just the two of you in that room.

who was she to you before the dream, do you know?
i don’t remember who she was really, just a young woman i was talking to.

a young woman you were talking to, whoever she was.

when the horse's head was finished, was there anything after that?
that’s where it ends for me. the horse’s head was the last thing.

so you're with a young woman by the autoclave in that room. she walks away to the other side, comes back with a block of glittering ice where her head was. it feels natural, she just stands there silent. the ice starts to melt, little channels opening, sharp edges rounding off, then it carves itself fast into a beautifully molded horse's head with eyes, ears and nostrils clear. it didn't feel frightening, more like carving than falling apart. then it ends there.

is that about right, or did i miss anything?
yeah that’s right. there isn’t anything else after the horse’s head, and the room didn’t feel scary, just ordinary.

an ordinary room, and that quiet, impossible thing happening in it. i've got it.

would you like to see it drawn?
yeah, i’d like that.

there's a few ways I could draw it for you. soft pencil on paper, a quiet hesitant touch like trying not to disturb the silence. cool wash of blue watercolor, like the memory melting at the edges, all cool and watery. textured black ink, solid black shapes and rough marks carving it out of darkness. or photographic realism, just as you saw it, a silent record of an impossible moment. which one feels closest, or would you describe your own way?
cool wash of blue watercolor, that feels closest

cool wash of blue watercolor, that's lovely. i'll start with you, then bring her in too, since you were both there.

how would you like to be drawn — as you are, or however i imagine you? you can tell me a little about yourself if you want.
however you imagine me is fine. i don’t mind.
i'm sketching you and the young woman and the room now. everything will appear on the right over the next minute or two. you can tell me if anything looks wrong once it's there.
the autoclave isn’t in it. the first one with her walking away and the horse head are close.

i'll make sure the autoclave is in there, that's the whole setting for it.

when you say the first one with her walking away and the horse head are close, do you mean those are two separate drawings, or one that has both moments?
i meant there were two that felt close, her walking to the far end and the horse head. not both in one picture.

got it, so two drawings feel close: the one of her walking to the far end, and the one with the horse head. and the autoclave should be there in both.

which one would you like me to work on first?
the horse head one first. i’d like that more complete.
the young woman and the room and you are up on the right now. does it look the way you remember?
it looks right. the ice is clearer than i expected but i like it.

i'm glad the ice feels right, even clearer than you expected.

everyone and everything is sketched now. i'll draw the moments of the dream in order, each carrying on from the ones before it, and they'll appear on the right as they're ready.
okay, first one’s up. it’s us by the autoclave before anything changes.

that's the moment before anything changes, then.

does it look the way you remember?
yeah, that’s right. maybe the room feels smaller in the drawing than it did.

the watercolor softness can make a room feel closer than it did, like the edges pressing in a little.

i can open it up a bit if you'd like.
no, leave it. it’s fine like that.
okay, i'll leave it just as it is.
what’s the second one? i can see her walking away now.
that's her walking away, yes. the rest of the moments are still being drawn, they'll appear on the right soon.
third one just came up. that’s her coming back with the ice block for a head. it looks right.
that's her coming back with the ice block for a head, exactly as you saw it. three more moments are still on the way, i'm drawing them now.
i’m looking at the third one again. she’s standing more stiff than she felt in the dream.

too stiff, got it. she felt more natural in the dream, just standing there quietly.

i'm redrawing her coming back with the ice block for a head, easing that stiffness. it'll appear on the right in a moment. the other moments are still being drawn too.
okay. the fourth one wasn't there a second ago, now it is. it’s the little channels starting to melt through.
the little channels starting to melt through. is that how you saw it?
close. it’s more like the lines were cutting in clean than dripping wet, if that makes sense.

i'm redrawing her coming back with her head gone, with your change. it will appear on the right.

the rest of the moments are still being drawn. two of the six are on the right so far: you and the young woman standing by the autoclave, and her walking away. the other four are still to come.
i can see the third one there now, and the fourth with the channels. the redraw of her head gone isn’t up yet.

the redraw's still being worked on, it'll be there in a moment.

once it's up, tell me if she stands the way she felt in the dream.
she’s up now. she stands more like she did, quiet and easy. that’s better.
good, i'm glad she stands easy now. the rest of the moments are still being drawn, they'll appear on the right soon.
the fifth one’s just come up. it’s the horse head nearly finished, with one of the eyes still soft. it fits.
that fits, one eye still soft like the dream almost finished but not quite. the last moment's still being drawn, it'll be on the right soon.
why are there only four up now? i thought there’d be five.

four is right for now. you and her by the autoclave, her walking away, her coming back with the ice for a head, and the little channels starting to melt. the other two are still being drawn, they'll be on the right soon.
